description.value: A functional MRI study investigated body image self-reflection in overweight and average-weight young women, comparing neural responses to fat, thin, and scrambled control body images and testing mediation by body dissatisfaction.

description.value: Participants viewed fat and thin female body images and vividly imagined someone comparing her body to the body in the picture; scrambled control images were viewed without the self-reflection instruction. The block-design run contained six fat, six thin, and six control blocks, with seven images per block.

description.value: Functional scans were realigned within and across runs, co-registered with anatomical data, normalized to Talairach space, resliced to 3 mm isotropic voxels, and spatially smoothed.

quotes: Functional scans were realigned within and across runs to correct for head motion, and co-registered with each participant’s anatomical data. Functional data were then normalized into standard stereotactic Talairach space, resliced into a voxel size of 3mm× 3mm × 3mm and smoothed with a 6mm (full width half maximum) Gaussian kernel to increase signal-to-noise ratio.
Data were analyzed using the Brain Voyager QX v2.3 software (Brain Innovation, The Netherlands).
